comparison.exact_conventions: Varju starts I_1^(0)=[0,2/3), width2/3^(n+1), N(n+1)=3N(n)+1; left,middle,spacer,right ordering; same fixed nonmixing set [0,2/9). His Borel [0,1] model differs only by null endpoints/completion from the local completed [0,1) model. Local proof supplies explicit conull inverse and left-reservoir placement.
comparison.independence: Different author and self-contained general-eigenfunction derivation, not an exercise or a reprint of Katok-Thouvenot. The argument uses Lusin approximation and propagation across the entire tower instead of first invoking ergodicity to normalize modulus.
comparison.argument_checked: Choose scaled f with positive measure {|f|>2}; epsilon<1/12 and that measure>10epsilon. A continuous Lusin approximant equal off a set of mass<epsilon is nearly constant on every fine physical level. Some level has bad proportion<2epsilon. Transport by all level iterates gives approximations lambda^(i-j)z on the entire tower. The {|f|>2} mass forces |z|>1 once the reservoir is small. The two return-overlap estimates each give a good intersection since 1/3-4epsilon>0, so |1-lambda^h|<2epsilon and |1-lambda^(h+1)|<2epsilon. Therefore lambda=1. The propagated single constant then approximates f outside sets whose measures tend to zero. For two such constants, the good sets intersect when their total error is<1, so the constants are Cauchy; their limit equals f a.e. This fills the routine final limiting sentence explicitly, without adding a missing eigenfunction step.
comparison.source_typos: The source has residual odometer bound j<2^n in the Chacon construction; the immediately surrounding definition and all subsequent Chacon formulas use j<N(n). Its displayed reservoir remainder 1/(2*3^n) is a harmless upper bound for the exact3^(-n-1). The local construction retains the exact formulas.
